reason: Both reached the correct child-lock diagnosis with no part recommendation, but Conversation 2 did so more efficiently: its first reply already asked the key diagnostic questions (power vs won't start, display symbols, lock icon) and it immediately identified the 'L' and gave the 3-second hold instruction, then confirmed with a heating test. Conversation 1 was clumsier: it claimed 'thanks for confirming the display is on' before the customer had said so, wasted a turn on a door-sensor question, and then repeated its lock question verbatim after the customer had already said they would try it, which reads as not listening. Conversation 2 also added useful prevention advice about the Stop/Cancel toggle and sticking buttons, whereas Conversation 1 ended with a generic closing.
